subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should OpenClaw fix this by making CLI health/status/stability RPC-first with read-only no-maintenance fallback, by adding a stricter gateway single-writer lease, or by requiring both?
rationale: The source boundary is clear enough to keep this open, but the permanent fix changes ownership between live gateway observability, doctor migrations, plugin-state probes, and operator recovery behavior.

options.title: RPC-first plus no-maintenance fallback
options.body: Status, health, and stability should ask the running gateway first, and any fallback file access while the gateway is active should be read-only with no journal, checkpoint, or migration work.

options.title: Gateway single-writer lease
options.body: The gateway should hold an explicit state DB ownership lease, and non-gateway processes should fail closed or route through gateway APIs for writes and maintenance.

options.title: Forensic harness first
options.body: Pause implementation until the reporter's corrupt DB bundle and a native runtime harness identify the exact OpenClaw helper or runtime interaction.

recommendation.title: RPC-first plus no-maintenance fallback
recommendation.body: Status, health, and stability should ask the running gateway first, and any fallback file access while the gateway is active should be read-only with no journal, checkpoint, or migration work.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision cuts across the DB-first runtime-state architecture introduced in the merged refactor they authored.
